title: Terraform keystore connector: HSM/KMS/Vault rotation + health prober
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a reusable Terraform module (redwood_keystore_connector) to standardize KMS/HSM and Vault integrations for Private (VPC) deployments. The module should support: AWS KMS and KMS multi-region aliases, GCP KMS, HSM proxying for on-prem hardware, Vault Transit and KV wrapping, secret replication bootstrap, rotation orchestration (scheduled + manual), and a lightweight health prober resource that exposes readiness/liveness signals to the operator. Deliverables: module code, Terratest acceptance suite, upgrade guide, CI integration, and an RFC for the rotation semantics and health probe API.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module accepts provider-agnostic inputs and exposes canonical outputs for keystore endpoints and IAM roles
Rotation plan supports scheduled rotation with dry-run option and safe rollback gates
Health prober returns stable /ready and /live endpoints that map to KV access + HSM ping + Vault token validity
Module passes Terratest scenarios: new deployment, rotation plan execution, simulated HSM failover, and upgrade from v1.0 to v2.0
CI implements plan/validate/apply (staged) using ephemeral infra in test account
Security review completed and KMS/HSM credentials never persisted in logs or state beyond provider best-practices
decisions: Use provider-agnostic interface: inputs use semantic names (keystore_type, primary_region, replicas) rather than provider-specific objects
Expose a rotation_job resource that calls a small Lambda/agent for deterministic rotation — avoids embedding rotation logic in Terraform apply
Health prober implemented as a small containerized binary that performs a minimal cryptographic op and verifies KV read; pod spec generated by Terraform
Use Terratest + real provider accounts for e2e coverage instead of mocking to catch provider-specific edge cases
Backward compatibility: provide upgrade script that migrates existing stateful resources and rotates aliases without downtime
tradeoffs: Embedding rotation logic in an external agent increases operational surface area but avoids long Terraform apply times and state conflicts
Using real provider accounts in tests increases test run cost and flakiness but yields actionable failures for infra edge cases
Providing both Vault and cloud-KMS support increases module complexity; modular subfolders will isolate provider-specific hooks
implementation_notes: Inputs: keystore_type (aws_kms | gcp_kms | hsm_proxy | vault_transit), primary_region, replica_regions, rotation_window_cron, rotation_dry_run, vault_mount_path, kms_key_alias
Rotation agent: simple Go binary that invokes provider SDKs or Vault API with change record in Dynamo/Firestore for leader election
Health prober: responds 200/503; probes: keystore_test_encrypt_decrypt, hsm_ping, vault_token_lookup
Tests: Terratest harness in /test/keystore_connector with parallel scenarios and teardown safety hooks
CI: add pipeline keystore-connector/integration with nightly runs and canary on merge to main
Docs: README must document upgrade steps, state migration, and emergency key revocation process
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Accidental key deletion or alias swap during rotation. Mitigation: rotation_job performs staged alias creation and validation on replicas before finalizing switch.
Risk: HSM provider outages in a region. Mitigation: multi-region aliases + transparent fallback to replica keystore endpoints.
Risk: Terraform state contains sensitive ARNs/IDs. Mitigation: mark sensitive outputs, use data sources for ephemeral tokens, and document recommended state encryption and locking.
Risk: Vault token expiry during probe. Mitigation: health prober attempts token refresh via auth path and exposes time-to-expiry metric
